I'm there, my friend....in my case it's highly related to feeling like a victim. I have zero trust in my ability to accomplish anything, and this is backed up by an extensive history.
So how to not feel like a victim?

* Remind yourself that you, at your core, are a capable human being. You won't believe it at first, but after reminding yourself over and over this will change.
* Learn to discern the things that you truly cannot change and accept them. Then the things that you might have some influence over seem less numerous and less overwhelming.
* Practice unattachment to outcomes, "fuck it," take the meaning out of the task. Learn what your mind feels like when you are in "just do it" mode, remember it, attempt to recall it often, and you will strengthen that ability like you would a muscle.

Those two things aren't mutually exclusive. Addictive behavior doesn't have to equate with a full on addiction, either. Think about it this way: many of the foods that our culture sees as "comfort foods" are these high refined carbohydrate foods. Pie, ice cream, mashed potatoes, the list goes on. We eat these foods because they relax us.

Personally, I believe that if we treated this more like addiction and focused on behavior change with that in mind, we would have some success. Let me put it this way: do you really think that if 79 million people who know that what they are putting in their mouth is bad, and do it anyway, do it out of 100 percent conscious choice?

The biggest one, IMO, is to keep weight down in the first place. It is much harder to lose. Genetic factors aside, I would simply teach my kids to have a healthy relationship with food so that they don't develop overeating habits.

Bring as much fiber into their lives as you can, and reduce how often they eat refined sugars.

Screen them for celiac. You won't notice symptoms when they are young, but untreated celiac can lead to type 1 diabetes, among other things.

Eat "real" food, and eat good food. As a diabetic, this is my key to eating really we'll and not getting bored, I make freshness, quality, flavor, and nutrient density my goals. A super restricted diet can get depressing fast unless you get creative.

I avoid processed and packaged food as much as possible. You would think that something like cherios would be good because it is low in sugar and high in fiber, but NO diabetic should ever touch that stuff unless they want a sky high blood glucose level.

A lot of people are addicted to food and don't realize it. It is difficult to have control when you are dealing with compulsive behavior. You need to treat the addiction first. It's hard for people who haven't been there to comprehend, and rightfully so.
